title: Skip-count forward and backward by 25s, 100s and 1000s

lesson.title: Big Jumps: Counting by 25s, 100s and 1000s

steps.say: You already know how to read and write big numbers like three thousand four hundred. Today we learn a speedy trick: instead of counting one at a time, we take big jumps of twenty five, one hundred, or one thousand.

Let's start with twenty fives, and think about quarters. A quarter is twenty five cents. One quarter, twenty five. Two quarters, fifty. Three quarters, seventy five. Four quarters, one hundred. So the twenty five pattern goes twenty five, fifty, seventy five, one hundred, and then it starts over: one hundred twenty five, one hundred fifty, one hundred seventy five, two hundred. Four jumps of twenty five always make one hundred.

Jumping by one hundred or one thousand is even easier, because only one digit changes. Say your class has raised three thousand four hundred dollars for a field trip. Jump forward by one hundred each week: three thousand five hundred, three thousand six hundred, three thousand seven hundred. Look closely, only the hundreds digit is climbing, four, five, six, seven. Everything else stays asleep.

Here is the mistake lots of kids make. Starting at three thousand nine hundred, they say the next one is three thousand ten hundred. That is not a real number. When the hundreds digit is already nine, one more hundred fills up a whole new thousand. So three thousand nine hundred plus one hundred is four thousand. Nine hundreds plus one hundred equals ten hundreds, and ten hundreds is one thousand, so the thousands digit goes up by one.

Backward works the same way, just going down. A snowy mountain trail marker says six thousand two hundred fifty metres. Count back by one thousand: five thousand two hundred fifty, four thousand two hundred fifty, three thousand two hundred fifty. Only the thousands digit drops, six, five, four, three. The two hundred fifty part never moves.

lesson.answer: Skip counting is big jumps: by 100 or 1000 only one digit changes, and four jumps of 25 make 100.

practice.question: Your class has raised two thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for a trip to Victoria, and each week you raise one thousand dollars more. Say the total after each of the next three weeks. Then, starting at three hundred dollars, count backward by twenty five three times.
practice.answer: Forward by 1000: three thousand seven hundred fifty, four thousand seven hundred fifty, five thousand seven hundred fifty. Backward by 25: two hundred seventy five, two hundred fifty, two hundred twenty five.
